standard_prerequisites: Tor independence of schemes as defined in Derived Categories of Schemes, and its extension to algebraic spaces via the strict-henselian local ring definition used in the source
Etale morphisms induce isomorphisms on strict local rings, and the functorial strict henselization description of etale local rings
Flat base change of Tor modules under henselization from More on Algebra
core_obligations: Equivalence of the intrinsic definition with the etale-local condition (2), and the implication (1) to (3)
Lifting geometric points through the etale diagram to reduce (3) to the definition

Agreement with the scheme definition: identify the strict henselian local ring of X over b with a strict henselization of the fibre tensor product, use flatness of that map and the Tor base-change formula to move Tor vanishing between the two readings

Converse over affine bases: flatness of the map on fibre tensor products plus image containment of the relevant primes turns space-level vanishing into vanishing of the localized Tor modules, then the cited More on Algebra lemma finishes
proof_roadmap: Prove (1) iff (2) and (1) implies (3) from the local-ring isomorphism property of etale morphisms
For (3) implies (1), lift the geometric points of the definition through W, U, V in turn
For (4), compare the space definition with the scheme definition via strict henselizations and the displayed Tor base-change identity
Run the converse over affines using flatness and the prime image argument, ending with the ring-level Tor independence lemma
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is a four-way equivalence making Tor independence of algebraic spaces etale-local on all three spaces and equal to the classical scheme notion (source lines 4964-5077, label lemma-tor-independent). The solver must control strict henselian local rings of fibres, prove flatness of the comparison maps, and move Tor vanishing across the base-change identity in both directions, including a prime-avoidance style image argument over affines; the reductions are not routine. Allowed background: the two Tor-independence definitions and the cited henselization and Tor lemmas, delivered as navigation pointers.
